Kevin Rideout, who was abducted by unknown assailants in Niamey, said to be in good health and in care of US officials

An American missionary who was kidnapped in Niger in October has been released, his organisation has said.

Serving in Mission International said Kevin Rideout “is in good health in the care of US officials” and would soon be reunited with his extended family.

guardian.description:
Man dies in Bas-Uele after travelling from Haut-Uele, as head of WHO says outbreak on track to be deadliest ever

The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has spread to a sixth province, officials have said, a day after the head of the World Health Organization said the outbreak was on track to surpass the deadliest in history, which killed at least 11,000 people more than a decade ago.

guardian.description:
Disciplinary proceedings under way after security concerns raised over reported visits to official residence

France has opened disciplinary proceedings against its ambassador to Central African Republic over allegations of misconduct, after claims he brought dozens of women into his official residence, raising potential security concerns.

guardian.title: Zambia elections haunted by ghost of incumbent president’s arch-rival
guardian.description:
Hakainde Hichilema is bidding for second term, but feud between him and family of Edgar Lungu, who died in 2025, continues

As Zambians go to the polls on Thursday, the ghost of the current president’s predecessor hangs over the elections.

Hakainde Hichilema, 64, is bidding for a second term leading the southern African country after defeating his arch-rival Edgar Lungu by a landslide in 2021.

guardian.title: At least 44 dead after overcrowded ferry capsizes on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe
guardian.description:
Operation under way to rescue dozens missing after boat overturned by waves at world’s largest human-made lake

At least 44 people have died after an overcrowded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe, police said.

The boat had a capacity of 90 people, but was carrying 114 adult passengers, five crew members and an unknown number of children, Zimbabwe’s civil protection unit (CPU) said earlier on Wednesday, citing ticket sales.

guardian.description:
Win is significant for region’s premier, Doug Ford, who blames protected zones for city’s traffic ills

The Ontario government is now free to rip out Toronto’s bike lanes on its busiest streets after the region’s top court ruled in favour of the province on Friday, overturning a lower court’s decision that decreed removal would violate constitutional rights.

guardian.description:
Grifols, which runs private chain of clinics, to temporarily stop taking donations after new government investigation

A chain of private plasma donation clinics in Canada has said it is pausing collections after the deaths of two donors and a new government investigation into potential unsafe practices.

guardian.description:

BP has answered Donald Trump’s call for oil companies to help rebuild Venezuela’s fossil fuel industry with new plans to develop a large offshore gasfield.

guardian.description:
Ángel Aguirre indicted in case that rocked Mexico and became symbol of its brutal cartel violence

guardian.description:
Female staff alleged company failed to maintain safe workplace, after allegations of sexual assault against pilot

The Canadian airline WestJet has agreed to pay C$4.5m (£2.4m) to settle a decade-long sexual harassment class action lawsuit levelled by its female flight attendants, who alleged the company failed to maintain a safe workplace.

guardian.description:
Shallow quake hit Indonesia’s Flores region early on Saturday, prompting thousands to seek higher ground after initial tsunami warning

A powerful 7.7-magnitude quake struck eastern Indonesia early on Saturday, the US Geological Survey said, sending thousands running in panic after authorities issued a tsunami warning.

The shallow quake hit Indonesia’s Flores region with a depth of 10km at 5.58am local time and was followed by two aftershocks, including one with a magnitude of 6.1

guardian.description:
Evacuation orders issued for 400,000 after flooding, landslide warnings and power outages in Chiba prefecture

At least five people have died in eastern Japan after “unprecedented” heavy rain that left nearly 7,000 stranded at Tokyo’s Narita airport and forced thousands to take refuge in government buildings.

guardian.title: Indonesia wildfires threaten orangutans rescued from animal traffickers
guardian.description:
Blaze fuelled by hot, dry and windy conditions comes within metres of West Kalimantan rehabilitation centre

Orangutans rescued from wildlife traffickers face a new threat from the record number of fires that have broken out in Indonesia in recent weeks.

Flames have come within metres of an animal rehabilitation centre in West Kalimantan as hot, dry and windy conditions have been amplified by a powerful El Niño and the human-driven climate crisis.

guardian.title: ‘Absolutely unacceptable’: Japan condemns visit by Vladimir Putin to disputed Kuril Islands
guardian.description:
Japanese PM says islands seized by Soviets late in second world war are part of her country under international law

The Japanese government has reacted angrily to Vladimir Putin’s first visit to the disputed Kuril Islands, which are claimed by both Tokyo and Moscow.

Japan’s foreign minister, Toshimitsu Motegi, summoned the Russian ambassador Nikolay Nozdrev, while the prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, called Putin’s actions “absolutely unacceptable”.

guardian.description:
Incheon airport had 38.39m international passengers in first half of 2026, as traffic diverted from Middle East hubs

South Korea’s Incheon airport has become the world’s busiest airport for international passengers, in part owing to disruption in the Middle East caused by the Iran war.

guardian.description:
Constitutional council says curbs infringe freedom of expression and privacy as president vows to rework legislation

France’s top court has blocked a ban on social media access for under-15s, ruling that it infringed freedom of expression and privacy.

The decision is a blow to President Emmanuel Macron as momentum builds around the world for Australian-style restrictions on children’s use of social media.

rfi.title: Fake accounts and false rumours drive new Ceuta crossing campaign
rfi.description: Calls for a new mass crossing into Ceuta, a Spanish enclave on Morocco's Mediterranean coast, have flooded Moroccan social media, with posts urging migrants to rush the border on Saturday. An RFI investigation found the campaign was fuelled by false rumours, suspicious accounts and signs of artificial amplification.

rfi.title: Law on assisted dying wins constitutional approval in France
rfi.description: France's Constitutional Council on Friday approved a law creating a right to assisted dying, removing the last major legal obstacle before the measure can be enacted and implemented.

rfi.title: Top French court scraps social media ban for children under 15
rfi.description: France's Constitutional Council struck down a law on Friday that would have banned children under 15 from using social media from September. The judges ruled that the measure placed a disproportionate restriction on freedom of expression and communication.

rfi.title: French firefighters threaten to strike over lack of resources
rfi.description: As wildfires continue to burn across France, representatives of firefighters' unions said they would go on strike in September to protest a lack of resources. Despite a meeting with the interior minister on Thursday, they say they are unhappy with the government's response so far.

rfi.title: US missionary kidnapped in Niger freed after more than nine months
rfi.description: American Kevin Rideout, who worked as a pilot for an evangelical organisation, has been freed after he was kidnapped in October 2025 in Niamey. His release comes as the security situation remains tense in Niger.

rfi.title: Zambia suspends vote counting nationwide citing violence
rfi.description: Zambia suspended vote counting nationwide on Friday following reports of violence in some districts, the electoral commission said.

rfi.title: Renewed fighting in Tigray raises risk of a wider regional war
rfi.description: A recent flare-up in tensions in Ethiopia's Tigray, including reports of heavy artillery battles and drone strikes, has raised fears of a return to war in the northern state – a conflict potentially stoked by foreign nations.

rfi.title: Farage wins UK by-election as Count Binface claims 'moral victory'
rfi.description: Hard-right British politician Nigel Farage reclaimed his seat in a by-election, according to the final tally Friday, though his main rival and joke candidate Count Binface took an larger than expected share of the ballot.

rfi.title: Europe faces rocket shortage by 2030 as satellite demand surges
rfi.description: Europe could face a shortage of rockets to launch its satellites by the end of the decade as demand for access to space rises sharply, the head of the European Space Agency has warned.

rfi.description: A controversial study analysing excess deaths during the Covid-19 pandemic has been retracted, after being widely criticised for lending credence to vaccine scepticism.

rfi.description: Mali's junta leader General Assimi Goïta has pardoned a French intelligence agent serving a 20-year prison sentence, a rare conciliatory move after years of strained relations between the west African nation and its former colonial ruler.

rfi.title: UN urges faster action as world falls behind on nature protection
rfi.description: The world is falling behind on its commitments to protect nature, the UN’s biodiversity chief has warned, ahead of a major international conference in Armenia aimed at accelerating action.

rfi.title: Romania shuts down nuclear plant due to low level of drought-hit Danube
rfi.description: Romania on Thursday began a complete shutdown of its only nuclear plant after levels of water in the River Danube – used to cool the site – fell to a record low, the national nuclear energy company said.

rfi.title: France and 30 other countries condemn Iran's executions of protestors
rfi.description: More than 30 countries, including France, the United Kingdom and Canada, have condemned Iran's use of capital punishment, saying in a joint statement on Wednesday the Islamic Republic was executing protesters to "silence dissent". Tehran accused its critics of hypocrisy.

rfi.title: Russia threatens retaliatory seizures of EU ships amid new sanctions push
rfi.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday threatened to seize ships belonging to European countries in retaliation for plans to sell off cargo seized from Russian "shadow fleet" vessels.

rfi.title: Morocco steps up border security over fears of new mass crossing into Ceuta
rfi.description: Morocco has stepped up security along its borders with the Spanish enclaves of Ceuta and Melilla after fresh calls appeared on social media urging migrants to attempt another mass crossing, weeks after tens of thousands rushed the frontier.

rfi.title: Sister act ushers underdogs Malawi into WAFCON final against Cameroon
rfi.description: Goals from sisters Tabitha and Temwa Chawinga on Wednesday gave tournament outsiders Malawi a 3-1 victory over Algeria, sending them to the Women's Africa Cup of Nations final – after they qualified for the tournament for the first time this year.

rfi.description: France’s foreign ministry has launched disciplinary proceedings against its ambassador to the Central African Republic, following allegations that he repeatedly brought young women to the official residence in Bangui and had sexual relations with some of them.

euronews.description: Arday made headlines when the university appointed him as its youngest black professor in 2023 but he since faced snowballing claims he plagiarised parts of his PhD thesis.

euronews.description: Ukraine has been targeting Russia's energy sites with drones and missiles for months, hoping to hit a vital source of revenue for the Russian army.

euronews.description: The paintings were taken by thieves from the villa of the Magnani-Rocca Foundation, near Parma in northern Italy, in a heist that lasted under three minutes.

euronews.title: Croatia wildfire near Omiš injures residents and disrupts holiday travel
euronews.description: A major wildfire near Omiš, around 25 kilometres south-east of Split, forced about 1,200 residents and tourists to evacuate overnight on Thursday and into Friday as strong winds drove the flames towards the coastal town.

euronews.description: Inspired by Hokusai’s 'The Great Wave off Kanagawa,' the carpet features more than 700,000 flowers and measures approximately 70 metres long and 24 metres wide.

euronews.description: At least one person was killed and 17 injured in a Russian airstrike on Kramatorsk in eastern Ukraine overnight, according to Ukraine’s State Emergency Service.

euronews.description: The Institute for the Study of War analysts framed the operation as evidence Ukraine can still mount coordinated, mechanised counterattacks after more than four years of largely static fighting.

lemonde.title: « En quarante-huit ans de métier, je n’ai jamais vu ça » : les fortes chaleurs précipitent les vendanges et font craindre de faibles rendements
lemonde.description: Les températures élevées de l’année 2026 ont accéléré le cycle de la vigne, déclenchant une récolte très précoce partout en France. Sécheresse et chaleur réduisent la taille et la quantité de jus des raisins.

lemonde.title: Interdiction des réseaux sociaux aux moins de 15 ans : le Conseil constitutionnel inflige un camouflet à l’exécutif
lemonde.description: Le Conseil constitutionnel a jugé qu’en s’appliquant à tous les réseaux sociaux et à tous les mineurs sans distinction, la loi enfreignait la liberté d’expression. Emmanuel Macron a chargé son gouvernement d’aboutir à un nouveau texte avant la fin de son mandat.

lemonde.title: « On est en train de perdre notre jeunesse » : dans le nord du Maroc, l’ombre des noyés de Ceuta
lemonde.description: A Tétouan, les familles se désespèrent après la mort de nombreux hommes qui ont tenté le passage à la nage jusqu’à l’enclave espagnole, fin juillet. Au total, plus de 140 d’entre eux auraient perdu la vie, selon une ONG marocaine. Malgré ces drames, beaucoup rêvent encore de gagner clandestinement l’Europe.

lemonde.title: Chez les opposants à Gianni Infantino, les grandes manœuvres sont lancées pour faire tomber le président de la FIFA
lemonde.description: Trois confédérations continentales, dont l’UEFA, aspirent à changer les statuts de la Fédération internationale de football afin de pousser vers la sortie son patron contesté, fragilisé par son projet avorté de création d’une société commerciale.

lemonde.title: « On m’a offert une poupée sur un poney, entourée de dessins de phallus » : le pot de départ graveleux de Marine, employée dans le BTP
lemonde.description: « Bon vent ! » (11/18). Elle ne supportait plus le sexisme ordinaire et l’ambiance potache de cette entreprise du BTP. Marine, 31 ans, n’avait encore rien vu…

lemonde.title: Loi d’urgence agricole : le Conseil constitutionnel valide la quasi-totalité du texte, y compris les volets controversés sur la réintroduction dérogatoire de pesticides interdits
lemonde.description: Cette dernière étape avant la promulgation pour un texte censé répondre à la colère agricole de l’hiver intervient au moment où l’agriculture française fait face à une sécheresse sans précédent, avec des conséquences dramatiques pour de nombreuses productions, végétales mais aussi animales.

lemonde.title: Le Conseil constitutionnel valide la loi sur la fin de vie, les établissements catholiques obtiennent leur « clause de conscience »
lemonde.description: Dans une décision rendue vendredi 14 août, l’institution assure « la liberté personnelle » d’un malade d’accéder à l’administration d’une substance létale à sa demande et après accord d’un médecin. En revanche, la décision exempte les établissements privés et associatifs de l’obligation de permettre la réalisation d’une aide à mourir dans leurs murs.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : plusieurs régions russes rationnent le carburant après les frappes ukrainiennes
lemonde.description: Le gouvernement russe a confirmé que l’approvisionnement des stations-service en carburant restait « tendu » dans plusieurs zones du pays. Selon un décompte de Bloomberg effectué à partir des déclarations publiques des deux camps, l’Ukraine a attaqué 11 des 34 grandes raffineries russes depuis le début du mois.

lemonde.title: Piratage du site des impôts : 678 000 usagers concernés, selon un nouveau bilan de la direction générale des finances publiques
lemonde.description: La DGFiP prévoit d’informer individuellement chaque victime du piratage et d’indiquer les précautions à prendre face à ce vol de données inédit.

lemonde.title: Cyclisme : le jeune Gallois Finlay Tarling tué dans un accident au Tour du Portugal
lemonde.description: Selon la télévision publique RTP, le coureur britannique de 19 ans de l’équipe NSN Development a été percuté pendant la 8ᵉ étape, vendredi, par une voiture circulant en sens inverse, un peu en retrait du peloton.

lemonde.title: Au Tchad, neuf opposants, dont Succès Masra, libérés après avoir été graciés par le président Mahamat Idriss Déby
lemonde.description: Ancien premier ministre et chef du principal parti d’opposition, Succès Masra purgeait depuis plus d’un an une peine de vingt ans de prison ferme. Les huit autres dirigeants de partis étaient condamnés car accusés de fomenter une insurrection.

lemonde.description: Le mouvement rebelle, soutenu par l’Iran, a par ailleurs affirmé avoir attaqué un site du géant pétrolier Aramco en Arabie saoudite, pays allié des Etats-Unis.

lemonde.description: Des dizaines d’autres personnes ont été blessées lors de cet assaut mené par les rebelles à Umm Arda, à environ 200 kilomètres au sud de la capitale, Khartoum. Plusieurs villes soudanaises sont le théâtre d’attaques de plus en plus intenses menées par les FSR.

lemonde.description: A Stourbridge, 19 maisons ont été complètement détruites et 18 endommagées dans l’incendie. Des habitants ont été évacués et 54 personnes traitées pour inhalation de fumée, dont 16 ont été hospitalisées.

Le chef des Transformateurs purgeait depuis plus d'un an une peine de 20 ans de prison ferme. Cette grâce ouvre-t-elle de nouvelles perspectives pour l'opposition ?

france24fr.title: Trump nie les inquiétudes concernant l'équipage du porte-avions Lincoln, en mer depuis huit mois
france24fr.description: Le président américain Donald Trump a catégoriquement écarté toute inquiétude au sujet de l'équipage du porte-avions Abraham Lincoln, en mission depuis plus de huit mois. Il a affirmé que le navire serait bientôt remplacé par un bateau similaire. Deux marins auraient tenté de se suicider, selon un média américain.

france24fr.title: Tunisie : les violences faites aux femmes persistent, 70 ans après le Code du statut personnel
france24fr.description: En Tunisie, le 13 août marque la Journée nationale de la femme. En 1956, le Code du statut personnel transformait profondément les droits des Tunisiennes. 70 ans plus tard, les féminicides et les violences faites aux femmes restent un fléau.

france24fr.title: Le jeune cycliste Finlay Tarling trouve la mort dans un accident au Tour du Portugal
france24fr.description: Le cycliste britannique Finlay Tarling, 19 ans, est mort vendredi dans accident survenu pendant la huitième étape du Tour du Portugal, a annoncé l'organisation de la course. L'évènement sportif a été suspendu "en signe de respect et de deuil".

france24fr.title: Non, le lac de Côme en Italie ne s’est pas vidé
france24fr.description: Le lac de Côme au nord de l’Italie aurait disparu à la suite d’une “rupture géologique”, annonce un reportage diffusé sur TikTok. C’est inexact : d’une part, les images de ce reportage ont été générées par intelligence artificielle. D’autre part, si le niveau du lac a effectivement baissé c’est-à-cause de la sécheresse, et les images satellites montrent que le lac de Côme est encore loin d’être tari.

france24fr.title: À Colombey, une bataille autour de la vente de la maison du général de Gaulle
france24fr.description: Un des petits-fils et héritiers du général de Gaulle s'est récemment opposé au rachat par l'État ou le département de la demeure où vécut le général, à Colombey-les-deux Églises. Qu'adviendra-t-il de cette maison historique ?

france24fr.title: Le Mali fait un geste envers Paris en graciant un agent français de la DGSE
france24fr.description: Le chef de la junte malienne, Assimi Goïta, a gracié Yann Vézilier, un agent du renseignement français arrêté en août 2025 et condamné à 20 ans de prison en juin 2026. Cette libération intervient après des années de fortes tensions entre Paris et Bamako.

france24fr.title: Au Népal, la difficile cohabitation entre humains et animaux sauvages
france24fr.description: En un demi-siècle, le Népal s’est imposé comme une référence mondiale en matière de conservation. Près de 20 % du territoire de ce petit État enclavé dans l’Himalaya est classé en zones protégées, fruit d’une politique de lutte contre le braconnage. Des espèces emblématiques comme le rhinocéros unicorne, autrefois au bord de l’extinction, ont pu être sauvés.

france24fr.title: Faux diacre "Frère Love" : une plaignante témoigne en Guadeloupe
france24fr.description: Une bien sombre affaire s'est déroulée entre la Guadeloupe et l'Île-de-France. Plusieurs personnes affirment être tombées sous l’emprise d'un certain "Frère Love", faux diacre catholique autoproclamé. L'une des plaignantes, "Sandrine" (le prénom a été modifié pour préserver son anonymat), rapporte avoir été victime d'un viol. Elle a accepté de nous parler de son calvaire. "Frère Love" nie toutes les accusations.

france24fr.title: Italie : l'Etna en éruption attire des milliers de touristes
france24fr.description: Les coulées de lave spectaculaires de l'Etna attirent des milliers de curieux sur les pentes du volcan sicilien. Jusqu'à 2 000 personnes tenteraient l'ascension chaque soir, selon un guide local. Face à cet afflux, les professionnels alertent sur les risques alors que le volcan reste en éruption.

france24fr.title: Ceuta : comment les réseaux sociaux alimentent la crise migratoire
france24fr.description: De nouveaux appels à franchir la frontière pour rejoindre Ceuta circulent depuis plusieurs jours sur les réseaux sociaux, suscitant l’inquiétude des autorités marocaines et espagnoles. Alors qu’un nouvel afflux migratoire est redouté le 15 août, ces messages, relayés notamment par de faux comptes, alimentent la confusion autour de la situation à la frontière. Comment expliquer cette campagne de désinformation et quels sont ses objectifs ? Les précisions de Romain Philips, journaliste à InfoMigra

france24fr.title: Le 15 août, la frontière ouverte à Ceuta ? Les faux appels sur les réseaux sociaux
france24fr.description: Après l'arrivée massive de migrants marocains les 30 et 31 juillet à Ceuta, l'enclave espagnole est à nouveau victime d'une campagne de désinformation sur les réseaux sociaux. Des messages provenant de faux comptes affirment que la frontière sera ouverte le 15 août, jour férié en Espagne. Les autorités marocaines et espagnoles ont renforcé les mesures de sécurité.

france24fr.title: CAN féminine 2026 : Cameroun-Malawi, une finale pour une première étoile
france24fr.description: ⚽ Le Malawi et le Cameroun s’affronteront dimanche en finale de la CAN féminine 2026. Les Lionnes Indomptables ont éliminé le Maroc, pays organisateur, aux tirs au but, tandis que le Malawi s’offre une première finale historique en battant l'Algérie. Dimanche soir, une nouvelle nation inscrira pour la première fois son nom au palmarès de cette compétition.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Le Conseil constitutionnel censure l'interdiction des réseaux sociaux aux moins de 15 ans
Le Conseil constitutionnel censure l'interdiction des réseaux sociaux aux moins de 15 ans
france24fr.description: Le Conseil constitutionnel a censuré vendredi l'interdiction des réseaux sociaux aux moins de 15 ans, invoquant "une atteinte disproportionnée" à leur liberté d'expression. Cette mesure est notamment défendue par le président Emmanuel Macron, qui vient de charger le Premier ministre de "travailler" à la rédaction d'une nouvelle version de l'interdiction.

france24fr.title: Cisjordanie : Washington dénonce le siège de maisons palestiniennes
france24fr.description: Depuis dimanche 9 août, des colons israéliens assiègent plusieurs maisons en Cisjordanie occupée. Les habitants sont privés de nourriture et d'eau potable. L'ambassadeur américain en Israël dénonce des "actions répugnantes".

france24fr.title: Sécheresse : Antoine Cadi décrypte les risques pour la France
france24fr.description: La France fait face à une situation de sécheresse particulièrement précoce et intense, alors que les autorités renforcent les mesures de restriction pour préserver la ressource en eau. Agriculture, biodiversité, usages domestiques : quels sont les secteurs les plus exposés et comment adapter les territoires à ces épisodes de sécheresse ? Antoine Cadi, directeur de la recherche et de l’innovation de CDC Biodiversité, répond à nos questions.

zeit.title: Indonesien: Schweres Erdbeben erschüttert indonesische Urlaubsinsel
zeit.description: Vor der indonesischen Insel Flores ist es zu einem Erdbeben der Stärke 7,7 gekommen. Bislang gibt es keine Informationen zu Verletzten.

zeit.title: Waldbrand bei Hürtgenwald: Wind dreht – Feuerwehr verlegt Einsatzzentrale wegen Rauchs
CDU-Nachwuchs Brandenburg: Junge Union berät nach Rücktritt über Reformen der Regierung
Fußball: Bayern-Frauen favorisiert im Supercup gegen Wolfsburg
Feuerwehr im Dauereinsatz: Löscharbeiten im Hürtgenwald gehen weiter
2. Fußball-Bundesliga: 277. Franken-Derby: FCN um Torjäger Zoma zu Gast in Fürth
Musik-Demo in Berlin: Techno-Parade unter verschärften Sicherheitsvorkehrungen
Wetter in Deutschland: Erst extreme Hitze, dann Wetterumschwung
zeit.description: Viele Regionen müssen sich am Samstag auf Höchstwerte bis 38 Grad einstellen. Intensivmediziner halten die offizielle Zahl der Hitzetoten für zu niedrig.

zeit.title: Steuerreform: SPD wirft Union »absurde Angriffe« vor
zeit.description: Die SPD-Fraktion fordert die Union auf, Kritik an den Steuerreformplänen des Bundesfinanzministers zu unterbinden. Ansonsten müsse der Kanzler ein Machtwort sprechen.

zeit.title: Irankrieg: Trump kündigt Übernahme der Straße von Hormus durch die USA an
zeit.description: Der US-Präsident sagt, er wolle die Straße von Hormus »bald« zu einem Territorium der USA erklären. Die Huthis greifen eine saudische Raffinerie an. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: US-Visa: USA entziehen Sohn von mexikanischem Ex-Präsidenten das Visum
zeit.description: Der Sohn des ehemaligen linken Staatschefs Andrés Manuel López Obrador kann nicht mehr in die USA einreisen. Präsidentin Sheinbaum vermutet politisches Kalkül.

zeit.title: Krieg gegen die Ukraine: Selenskyj warnt vor Engpässen bei weltweiter Lebensmittelversorgung
zeit.description: Der ukrainische Präsident sieht die internationalen Lebensmittelketten durch russische Angriffe bedroht. Russland meldet Engpässe beim Benzin. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Moskau: Russland erklärt Forschungsstelle Osteuropa für »unerwünscht«
zeit.description: Die russische Justiz stuft die Forschungsstelle für Osteuropa der Universität Bremen als unerwünschte Organisation ein. Eine Begründung für die Entscheidung gab es nicht.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Iran: Keine Entscheidung über neue Verhandlungen mit den USA +++ Iran nach Trump-Vorstoss: Strasse von Hormuz gehört uns
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: Audrey Werro trotzt der emotionalen Achterbahnfahrt und wird souverän Europameisterin über 800 m
nzz.description: Die 22-jährige Schweizerin lässt an den Leichtathletik-EM in Birmingham ihrer grössten Konkurrentin Keely Hodgkinson keine Chance. Es ist die fünfte Medaille für die Schweiz an den EM.

nzz.title: Deutscher Sprinter Owen Ansah gewinnt EM-Titel über 200 Meter –Schweizer Timothé Mumenthaler holt Bronze
nzz.description: Nach Bronze über 100 Meter setzt Owen Ansah einen drauf. Er gewinnt den Titel über 200 Meter und holt die erste Medaille eines deutschen Mannes über die Distanz seit 40 Jahren. Doch eine Sperre droht.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Migrationskrise in Europa: Zivile Helfer entdecken elf Leichen vor libyscher Küste +++ Zahl der irregulären Grenzübertritte in die EU sinkt laut Frontex deutlich
nzz.description: Über die griechischen Inseln, die Balkanroute oder den Ärmelkanal versuchen neben den Fluchtbewegungen aus der Ukraine noch immer täglich Migranten, unter Lebensgefahr nach Europa zu gelangen.

nzz.title: Jason Arday ist laut britischen Medienberichten tot
nzz.description: Der einst als jüngster schwarzer Professor in Cambridge gefeierte Wissenschafter ist im Alter von 41 Jahren tot aufgefunden worden. Erst vor wenigen Tagen war er nach Plagiatsvorwürfen von seinem Posten zurückgetreten.

nzz.title: Junger Brite verunglückt nach Sturz an der Portugal-Rundfahrt
nzz.description: Laut dem portugiesischen TV-Sender RTP kollidierte Finlay Tarling mit einem entgegenkommenden Auto.

nzz.title: EU-freundliche Ständeräte gegen Skeptiker: Aussenpolitiker wollen Lohnschutz ausbauen
nzz.description: Die aussenpolitische Kommission stellt sich beim neuen Vertragspaket gegen die ständerätlichen Wirtschaftspolitiker.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Wie beliebt ist Donald Trump?
nzz.description: Täglich aktualisierte Umfragewerte zeigen, wie die Amerikaner derzeit zur Amtsführung ihres Präsidenten stehen. Eine Übersicht in Grafiken.

nzz.title: INTERAKTIV - Gasspeicher liegen deutlich unter Normalniveau – die aktuellen Zahlen zur Energieversorgung in Deutschland
nzz.description: Wie wirken sich Energiewende und globale Krisen auf Strom- und Gaspreise aus? Hier gibt es jeden Tag die aktuellen Zahlen.

nzz.title: Ein Bergführer ist schuld am Tod zweier junger Menschen. 2023 kamen sie an der Gstelliwang in einer Lawine ums Leben
nzz.description: Das Regionalgericht in Thun folgte inhaltlich dem Gutachten des Experten und spricht den Bergführer der mehrfachen fahrlässigen Tötung schuldig.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Trumps zweite Amtszeit: Antisemitismus-Klage gegen Harvard abgewiesen
nzz.description: Donald Trump regiert zum zweiten Mal als amerikanischer Präsident – mit weitreichenden innen- und aussenpolitischen Folgen. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: Neuer Eklat in der Causa Dittli: Das Parteipräsidium lässt seine Staatsrätin fallen
nzz.description: Die Führung der Mitte Waadt will bei den kantonalen Wahlen 2027 nicht mehr mit der umstrittenen Valérie Dittli antreten. In den kommenden Tagen könnte es zum Showdown um die Parteibasis kommen.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Bald kann jeder autonome KI-Agenten auf seine Feinde hetzen. Der Angriff auf Taiwan markiert einen gefährlichen Wendepunkt
nzz.description: Autonome KI-Agenten helfen im Cyberkrieg den Angreifern mehr als den Verteidigern. Westliche Demokratien müssen nun ihre digitale Wehrhaftigkeit und den Schutz kritischer Infrastrukturen zur zentralen Aufgabe der nationalen Sicherheit machen.

nzz.title: Schwerer Unfall auf der A2: Seelisbergtunnel wieder geöffnet
nzz.description: Wegen eines Unfalls war der Verkehr vor dem Seelisbergtunnel auf der A 2 in beide Richtungen gesperrt.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Hitze in Europa: Spanien kämpft gegen zwei Grossbrände und evakuiert weitere Einwohner +++ In Hürtgenwald wird Gegenfeuer zur Brandbekämpfung eingesetzt
nzz.description: Wo ist es zurzeit besonders heiss? Und was sind die Auswirkungen auf die Menschen und die Umwelt? Die neuesten Meldungen über Hitzerekorde, Dürren und Brände in Europa.

observador.title: 2h. PM critica censura moderna e que só se fala de polémicas
observador.description: Posição do Primeiro-Ministro no discurso dos 50 anos da Festa do Pontal, que ficou marcado por grandes novidades. Ainda, Donald Trump admite declarar o Estreito de Ormuz como território dos EUA.

observador.title: 1h.André Ventura acusa PM de estar desligado dos portugueses
observador.description: Presidente do Chega diz que Luís Montenegro confundiu as grandes reformas do Governo com a realidade do país. Ainda neste noticiário, NSN Development Team vai abandonar Volta a Portugal em Bicicleta.

observador.title: Sindicato pede mediação para negociar contratação coletiva
observador.description: Sindicato afirma que "a má-fé negocial demonstrada pelas associações patronais ao longo do último ano conduziu a este pedido de mediação estatal, remetido à Direção-Geral do Emprego.

observador.title: Coimbra reabilita Centro de Interpretação do Paul de Arzila
observador.description: A Câmara de Coimbra liderou a candidatura aprovada ao Fundo Ambiental. Condeixa-a-Nova obteve igual financiamento para renovar a exposição interpretativa.

observador.title: Sara Correia e Camané no Festival Fado no Rio de Janeiro
observador.description: Sara Correia e Camané estarão presentes no Festival Fado a 6 de novembro. Será ainda inaugurada no Vivo Rio a exposição "Os Bairros de Lisboa", que conta a história de bairros emblemáticos da cidade.

observador.title: A vida falsa e a morte verdadeira de Jason Arday
observador.description: Em suma, Jason Arday era um aldrabão. Toda a história dele é uma sucessão de mentiras cujo descaramento cresceu em proporção directa à importância que lhe deram.

observador.title: O eclipse do sol e a assunção de Maria
observador.description: “Apareceu no Céu um grande sinal: uma Mulher vestida de Sol, com a Lua debaixo dos seus pés, e uma coroa de doze estrelas sobre a sua cabeça” (Ap 12, 1)

observador.title: Aljubarrota: quando Portugal decidiu existir
observador.description: É por isso que Aljubarrota não pertence apenas à história militar. Pertence à história da soberania. Foi o momento em que Portugal disse que a geografia não bastava para o definir.

observador.title: Dificuldades com cheiros
observador.description: Não reconhecemos os cheiros entre amostras e por catálogo; reconhecemo-los como reconhecemos uma pessoa que encontramos num sítio inesperado.

observador.title: Sporting x Vitória. "Disciplinarmente não correu bem"
observador.description: Nota 5 para equipa de arbitragem liderada por David Silva. "Nem Sporting, nem Vitória podem queixar-se da arbitragem" num jogo em que, mesmo sem grandes lances, houve falhas na gestão disciplinar.

observador.title: As notícias das 00h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Trump pondera declarar Ormuz como "território dos EUA"
observador.description: O Presidente dos EUA afirma que pondera declarar o Estreito de Ormuz como "um território dos EUA", depois de "derrotar o Irão".

observador.title: Garrett e as Folhas Caídas ou Bashô no Campo Grande
observador.description: A beleza não apaga as feridas. Redime-nos de outra maneira, mais discreta e mais verdadeira: impede que a realidade se reduza à sua evidência dolorosa.

observador.title: "Na segunda parte a energia caiu, ficámos muito macios"
observador.description: Depois de mais um jogo que se tornou sofrido, Borges disse que a equipa está a passar por "dores de crescimento" e pediu aos adeptos. Leão leva 95 minutos sem rematar nas segundas partes.

observador.title: A Lisboa dos mortos-vivos
observador.description: Na Mouraria, um espaço destinado ao consumo fumado teve mesmo de ser desactivado por excesso de procura. Isto é real. Não fechou porque não havia consumidores. Fechou porque havia consumidores a mais.

observador.title: Educação para todos. Para quase todos...
observador.description: Uma criança com Necessidades Educativas Especiais não pode ser tratada como uma variável que se encaixa quando houver disponibilidade.

observador.title: O centenário de Fidel Castro e uma revolução que é uma marca
observador.description: Cuba não é apenas uma experiência romântica de resistência ou a fotografia de Che Guevara. É uma história de prisões políticas, censura, perseguição de dissidentes e ausência de liberdade.

observador.title: Ética: a primeira instituição da democracia
observador.description: Quando os cidadãos percecionam que os princípios cedem perante as conveniências, afastam-se. E nesse afastamento crescem a descrença, o populismo e a radicalização.

spiegel.title: Feuer im Hürtgenwald: Feuerwehr muss Einsatzzentrale wegen Rauch verlegen – Löscharbeiten gingen in der Nacht weiter
spiegel.description: Der Hürtgenwald in der Eifel steht weiter in Flammen. Die Einsatzleitung der Feuerwehr musste umziehen, um dem Qualm auszuweichen. Die Brandbekämpfer rechnen mit einem Einsatz, der noch Tage dauern wird.

spiegel.title: Bauarbeiter finden in Belgien Gold im Wert von neun Millionen Euro
spiegel.description: Ungläubigkeit und Staunen – so beschreibt ein Arbeiter den Moment, als sein Team beim Verlegen eines Abwasserrohrs auf einen Goldschatz stieß. Neun Millionen Euro, eingemauert in einer Kellerwand in einem Haus in Belgien.

spiegel.title: Trump will Straße von Hormus zum US-Territorium erklären
spiegel.description: Der US-Präsident hatte im Irankrieg einen schnellen Sieg versprochen, doch ein Frieden scheint in weiter Ferne. Seine neue Ankündigung zur Straße von Hormus dürfte den Konflikt kaum entschärfen.

spiegel.title: Selena Gomez: Start-up wird auf Millionen verklagt
spiegel.description: Gemeinsam mit ihrer Mutter gründete Selena Gomez »Wondermind«, eine Plattform für mentale Gesundheit. Nun verklagen zwei Investoren die Gründerinnen. Der Vorwurf: Sie hätten mit falschen Versprechen gelockt.

spiegel.title: USS »Abraham Lincoln«: Donald Trump findet, Einsatz auf Flugzeugträger dauert »noch nicht lange genug«
spiegel.description: Seit mehr als acht Monaten ist der Flugzeugträger im Nahen Osten, es gibt Versorgungsengpässe, die Besatzung ist offenbar am Limit. Ein Problem sieht der US-Präsident darin nicht.

spiegel.title: Helmut Lethen: Kulturwissenschaftler im Alter von 87 Jahren gestorben
spiegel.description: Mit seiner Epochenstudie »Verhaltenslehren der Kälte« wurde er in den Neunzigerjahren zum Kultautor. Jetzt ist Helmut Lethen im Alter von 87 Jahren gestorben.

spiegel.title: Leichtathletik-EM: Owen Ansah holt Gold, Emil Agyekum und Shanice Kraft Silber
spiegel.description: Sprinter Owen Ansah hat in Birmingham das dritte EM-Gold für das deutsche Team gewonnen. Fraglich bleibt, ob er den Titel behalten darf. Jeweils Silber holten Hürdenläufer Emil Agyekum und Diskuswerferin Shanice Kraft.

spiegel.title: Jason Arday: Cambridge-Professor nach Plagiatsvorwürfen tot aufgefunden
spiegel.description: Er war der jüngste schwarze Professor an der Eliteuniversität Cambridge, nach Plagiatsvorwürfen legt er sein Amt nieder. Nun ist Jason Arday tot. Er wurde 41 Jahre alt.

spiegel.title: Matisse, Renoir und Cézanne: Drei aus Museen in Italien gestohlene Gemälde wieder aufgetaucht
spiegel.description: Mitten in der Nacht verschwinden drei Kunstwerke, zusammen sind sie fast zehn Millionen Euro wert: Nach monatelangen Ermittlungen kann die italienische Polizei nun einen Erfolg vermelden.

spiegel.title: Stendal: AfD-Politiker verfolgt 14-Jährigen mit Baseballschläger
spiegel.description: In Stendal haben zwei Jugendliche ein AfD-Wahlplakat beschädigt. Dabei lauerten ihnen zwei Politiker der rechtsextremen Partei auf. Ein 14-Jähriger wurde verletzt. Die Polizei ermittelt.

spiegel.title: Schwimm-EM: Isabel Gose, Angelina Köhler und Maya Werner bejubeln Medaillen
spiegel.description: Ex-Weltmeisterin Angelina Köhler versöhnt sich mit Paris. Isabel Gose steht zum vierten Mal auf dem Podest, wieder neben Maya Werner. Für Olympiasieger Lukas Märtens war sein Rennen vorbei, »ehe ich gefühlt im Wasser war«.

spiegel.title: Reit-WM 2026: Debütantin Katharina Hemmer holt überraschend Bronze
spiegel.description: Zwei Tage nach dem WM-Titel im Team sichert sich Katharina Hemmer die Bronzemedaille im Grand Prix Special. Isabell Werth muss sich mit Rang vier begnügen. Auch die Vielseitigkeitsreiter sind auf Medaillenkurs.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: So verlief die Flucht im Catering-Container
spiegel.description: Mit einem Täuschungsmanöver wurde US-Präsident Trump vor einem angeblich drohenden iranischen Anschlag in Sicherheit gebracht. Der Rest seiner Delegation blieb als argloser »Köder« zurück. Die Rekonstruktion.

spiegel.title: Sachsen-Anhalt: Wie Campact mit drei Millionen Euro gegen die AfD mobilisiert
spiegel.description: Die Plattform Campact will mit Millionenspenden eine Alleinregierung der AfD verhindern, indem sie SPD und Grünen den Einzug in den Landtag sichert. Ein ähnlicher Aufruf war schon einmal erfolgreich.

spiegel.title: Kleingarten: »Sogar Wessis sind Menschen« – Streit im Schrebergarten - SPIEGEL TV
spiegel.description: Ein Schrebergarten soll ein Ort der Idylle sein. Nicht so im beschaulichen Teil Leipzigs. Hier eskaliert der Klassenkampf. Es geht um einen Parkplatz samt Gebühren, geklauten Strom und um jemanden, der eine Mauer errichten will.

spiegel.title: FC Liverpool: Jeff Bezos sichert sich Minderheitsbeteiligung
spiegel.description: Als Teil eines Konsortiums hat sich der Amazon-Milliardär beim FC Liverpool eingekauft – für einen Betrag von bis zu 1,8 Milliarden Euro. Fans machen sich Sorgen um die Zukunft des Premier-League-Clubs.

spiegel.title: Nathalie Pohl: Extremschwimmerin erreicht nach vier Tagen und 200 Kilometern Köln
spiegel.description: Am Dienstag ist Nathalie Pohl in den Main gesprungen, an diesem Freitag ist die 31-Jährige nun in Köln aus dem Rhein gestiegen. Mit der Aktion will Pohl für die Sicherheit junger Schwimmer werben.

spiegel.title: Düsseldorf: Frau wegen Hilfe für IS-Terroristen verurteilt
spiegel.description: Eine 43-Jährige hat jahrelang europaweit gefangene IS-Terroristen und Anhänger unterstützt, unter anderem mit Geld. Nun wurde die Deutsche verurteilt.

letemps.title: L'époustouflante Audrey Werro, miraculée en demi-finale, devient championne d'Europe du 800 mètres
letemps.description:
La Fribourgeoise de 22 ans a remporté sa première médaille d'or en élite ce vendredi à Birmingham. Après avoir été repêchée suite à une chute au tour précédent, elle confirme son statut de patronne de la distance et valide tous ses choix de carrière

Forcément, le souvenir de la chute au tour précédent devait être là, dans un coin de sa tête. Au départ de la finale du 800 mètres des Champi

letemps.title: Timothé Mumenthaler doit se contenter de la médaille de bronze sur le 200 mètres des Championnats d'Europe

phys-org.title: 'Starwashing': How space companies use the greenwashing playbook while causing environmental damage
phys-org.description: From launchpads to low Earth orbit and beyond, space companies and their affiliates are deploying a familiar marketing tactic—with a new twist. In a space economy projected to reach US$1.8 trillion by 2035, they sell space exploration narratives by appealing to a desire to expand humankind beyond Earth—while downplaying or omitting the negative repercussions for Earth and the space environment. Welcome to the age of starwashing.

phys-org.title: The false and the furious: We aren't just bothered by different beliefs—we're bothered when we think others are wrong
phys-org.description: Why do disagreements about vaccines, climate change or elections often feel so personal? Our research suggests it is not simply because other people have different beliefs. It is because we think those beliefs are mistaken.

phys-org.title: Green roofs can help cool cities in the summer heat, but building them is only the first step. Many don't survive
phys-org.description: As summer temperatures soar across the United States and Europe, cities are being forced to confront the difficult reality that they're getting dangerously hot.

phys-org.title: Airborne observatory improves views of solar corona during cloud-covered eclipse
phys-org.description: Using unique equipment installed on NASA's WB-57 aircraft flying above heavy clouds off the coast of Iceland, a Southwest Research Institute-led team successfully observed a total solar eclipse on Wednesday. The high-altitude jet followed the moon's shadow at 50,000 feet (15,000 meters) to take measurements of the solar corona in nine different wavelengths, ranging from visible to infrared light.

phys-org.title: Wheat gene behind Hessian fly resistance cloned after 50-year search
phys-org.description: Researchers at the University of Maryland and their collaborators have cloned a gene that makes wheat resistant to feeding by Hessian fly larvae and demonstrated its direct interaction with a protein produced by the insect. The research breaks through a longstanding barrier to understanding and engineering pest resistance in wheat. It is described in a research paper published Aug. 14, 2026, in the journal Science Advances.

phys-org.title: Unlocking the past: New method helps gain insights into old tissues
phys-org.description: A book sits atop a table. Although it's closed, its title, "Encyclopedia of Human Tissue," promises untold secrets. Perhaps with this book, you can learn about different cell types and what they look like under normal conditions or conditions of disease. Maybe you can learn how gene expression differs in the cells of younger and older people, or whether different patients' cells respond differently to the same treatments.

phys-org.title: Europe's mountain summits are warming—vegetation is responding in surprisingly different ways
phys-org.description: Decades of climate change have not left Europe's mountain vegetation unscathed. However, the changes observed do not always match expectations. As a new international study by a research team led by researchers from the University of Vienna, the Austrian Academy of Sciences and the BOKU University shows, alpine vegetation has shifted significantly towards warmth-associated species. However, the direct link between this so-called thermophilization and local warming is surprisingly weak. The

phys-org.title: Engineered microbe speeds CO₂ capture and recovers critical metals
phys-org.description: A genetically engineered bacterium can rapidly break down one of Earth's most abundant minerals, opening a promising new pathway for simultaneously removing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and recovering critical elements used in electric vehicle batteries, according to new Cornell research.

phys-org.title: Bones of medieval kings saved from Spanish wildfire
phys-org.description: Firefighters raced to save a 1,000-year-old monastery in northeastern Spain on Friday as a growing wildfire prompted the hasty removal of the bones of medieval monarchs buried there.

phys-org.title: Cell biochemistry beyond membranes: Condensate physics reveals general rules for chemical responses
phys-org.description: Basic biology courses teach that cells contain organelles—such as the nucleus, mitochondria and Golgi apparatus—set apart by lipid membranes to get things done. Recent cell biology research has revealed another organizational principle at work in cells across all orders of biology.

phys-org.title: Bound gravitational waves inspired by photonic systems
phys-org.description: When one mentions "waves," we immediately think of a perturbation that propagates. This applies to waves on the shore, sound waves in the air or electromagnetic waves that we use to transmit information via optical fibers. The same idea of propagating perturbations applies to gravitational waves (GWs), which entered the mainstream media a decade ago after their first direct detection. These are perturbations of the elastic fabric that we are all embedded in, called spacetime.

phys-org.title: Cells pulse together as they grow—and malignant cells pulse the longest
phys-org.description: Epithelial cells are the tiny shields that line and protect our bodies. In a developing embryo, epithelial cells grow, divide and move into positions to form the outer layers of our skin and the surfaces of our organs and blood vessels. When we scrape our skin, suffer an internal tear or undergo surgery, epithelial cells migrate to the site of injury to heal a wound. And when epithelial cells go haywire, they can turn malignant and spread through the body as cancer.

phys-org.title: Guangzhou crucibles provide earliest direct evidence of brass-making in East Asia
phys-org.description: For centuries, scholars have read ancient documents describing the production of brass in 10th-century A.D. China. The problem was that the earliest physical evidence of brass production would be found nearly 600 years later, in the 16th century A.D.

phys-org.title: Wildfires have destroyed an area of protected tropical forest twice the size of Wales since 2001, study reveals
phys-org.description: Over 4 million hectares (9.9 million acres) of protected tropical forest—an area double the size of Wales—have been lost to wildfires since 2001.

phys-org.title: Early settlement dynamics in the Pacific revealed through ancient DNA
phys-org.description: New genetic analyses of ancient human skeletons from western Remote Oceania are shedding light on the complex history of settlement in this vast Pacific region over the past 3,000 years. With island nations such as Vanuatu, Fiji and Tonga, the region is home to societies with a remarkably high degree of linguistic and cultural diversity.

phys-org.title: Constipation is common in astronauts—blood tests provide new answers
phys-org.description: For astronauts in space, constipation is a well-known problem. But why this happens has long been unclear. Now, a new study from the University of Copenhagen in collaboration with NASA provides an idea of what happens in the stomach without the influence of gravity.

phys-org.title: A new way to beat jet lag? Engineered cells speed circadian adjustment
phys-org.description: Adjusting to a new time zone or work schedule can leave the body's internal clock out of sync for days, contributing to sleep disruption, metabolic changes and other health consequences. Researchers at Rice University and Northwestern University have developed an implantable cell therapy that may help the body adapt more quickly to these disruptions.

phys-org.title: X-band radar data sharpen simulation of westerly weak tornado
phys-org.description: Tornadoes are among the most destructive weather phenomena on Earth. Their small scale, short life cycle and sudden onset make them extremely difficult to predict. This challenge is amplified for weak tornadoes embedded within midlatitude westerly flows, which often hide in plain sight with faint signals. Improving the simulation capability for these events is vital for reducing disaster risk in highly vulnerable regions such as the Pearl River Delta.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: What Should Be Done About Asia’s Undervalued Currencies?
proj-syn.description: Those who worry that the renminbi, yen, and won are undervalued vis-à-vis the dollar are usually focused on the large trade and current-account surpluses that China, Japan, and Korea run with the US. But coordinated intervention in currency markets will not address the fundamentals underlying these imbalances.

proj-syn.title: How Corporations Can Mitigate an AI Jobocalypse
proj-syn.description: Even if AI-related job displacement is less severe than many feared, corporations will need to be enlisted in minimizing its effects in the name of social solidarity. To that end, governments should consider what policy incentives are in place, and large employers should consider their own long-term interests.

proj-syn.title: The Making and Remaking of Chinese Totalitarianism
proj-syn.description: For decades, the West assumed that economic growth would turn China into a more open, liberal society, much as it did South Korea and Taiwan. Instead, China’s totalitarian institutions proved remarkably resilient, surviving decades of reform and reasserting themselves under President Xi Jinping.

proj-syn.title: Let’s Not Forget Multilateral Institutions
proj-syn.description: The roadmap for middle-power action that Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Finnish President Alexander Stubb recently laid out calls for countries that share interests to create ad hoc coalitions. But to be effective, these coalitions must work as much as possible within existing multilateral institutions.

proj-syn.title: The Real Competitiveness Test
proj-syn.description: The balance of global investment has shifted dramatically over the past three decades, with China emerging as the leading destination for productive capital. Europe and the United States can still narrow the gap, but only by making it cheaper and easier to build, operate, and innovate.

proj-syn.title: Our AI, Your Problem
proj-syn.description: The debate over whether European firms should use a Chinese state-directed model or one built by a private US firm threatens to distract from Europe’s most pressing problem, which is that it has no seat at either table. To preserve its own sovereignty, the continent must create a third option for itself.

proj-syn.title: Chile’s Boring Conservative President
proj-syn.description: Rather than governing like a pugnacious populist or a ruthless pragmatist, Chile’s new president, José Antonio Kast, has adopted an old-school center-right agenda and governing style reminiscent of the 1980s. Yet even this potentially safer approach comes with its own risks and costs.

proj-syn.title: Europe Failed the Ceuta Test
proj-syn.description: The current migration crisis is eating away at the solidarity on which the European Union depends, fueling the rise of the far right and pushing leaders to adopt increasingly hardline policies. But the Ceuta debacle shows why such measures cannot address the deeper forces driving migration.

proj-syn.title: The Legacy of Zhu Rongji
proj-syn.description: Zhu Rongji’s personal history and political challenges made it highly unlikely that he would rise to the pinnacle of Chinese politics. Once there, he implemented many of the reforms that turned the country into an economic powerhouse.

proj-syn.title: The Twilight of the ICC
proj-syn.description: Born amid the euphoria of the West’s Cold War victory, the International Criminal Court embodied the aspiration that international law could transcend politics. But the ICC always represented victors’ justice, and it was never equipped to operate in a world shaped by Machtpolitik.

proj-syn.title: Will Latin America Embrace Guerrilla Geopolitics?
proj-syn.description: The resurgence of guerrilla warfare in Ukraine and Iran has underscored the potential benefits of asymmetric action in today’s increasingly multipolar world. Latin America, in particular, should consider how to leverage its many strengths to remedy its relatively weak position on the global stage.

proj-syn.title: China’s Biggest Weakness on AI
proj-syn.description: When a state can credibly promise that labor displacement will not mean destitution, workers and their representatives are more likely to accept technological change. But since China can promise no such thing, its lack of a robust welfare state has emerged as a fundamental weakness in the broader AI race.

proj-syn.title: The Monetary Roots of Political Extremism
proj-syn.description: While the global economy generates unprecedented wealth for plutocrats like Elon Musk, it is, by design, highly unequal, dangerously over-indebted, prone to recurring financial crises, and ecologically disastrous. In such a context, radical reforms will be needed, beginning with the rejection of money as a commodity.

proj-syn.title: The Return of the Power Trust
proj-syn.description: A century ago, the US power industry was dominated by sprawling, heavily indebted holding companies until their collapse forced the federal government to break them up. Now, the pattern is repeating, with mega-mergers and buyouts advancing a debt-heavy business model at the expense of households and communities.

proj-syn.title: Morocco’s Bet on Targeted AI
proj-syn.description: Rather than join the global race for computing power, Morocco has focused on building sovereignty over its data, talent, and uses of AI, because technological power will be measured by usefulness, not by domination. This strategy calls for the country to embrace innovation without ceding its identity to foreign models.

proj-syn.title: Dude, Where’s My Recession?
proj-syn.description: Despite a series of major negative shocks, some of them unprecedented, the US economy continues to grow in line with its estimated long-run potential. Yet given obvious and mounting risks, from debt-financed speculation to geopolitical tensions, the appearance of resilience should not be confused with the real thing.

proj-syn.title: The Rise of the Token Economy
proj-syn.description: Millions of people continuously generate the raw material on which AI is trained, yet almost none shares in the wealth it creates. This underscores the need for data cooperatives representing internet users, creators, and other rights holders to negotiate access to the content being fed to large language models.

proj-syn.title: Excess Savings Are Driving the New China Shock
proj-syn.description: The current China shock combines continued supply upgrading with an absorption problem: the decline in property and related investment has reduced domestic demand, but national saving remains very high. The result is a larger savings-investment surplus that spills into net exports.
